name: Raffles Hotel Singapore
insider_take: Colonial grandeur meets modern luxury in Singapore's most legendary address, where literary legends once penned masterpieces and the Singapore Sling was born.
whats_special: This iconic 1887 hotel is where Somerset Maugham wrote, Rudyard Kipling stayed, and Charlie Chaplin honeymoned. The famous Long Bar is the birthplace of the Singapore Sling cocktail, created in 1915. After a meticulous $500 million restoration, the hotel seamlessly blends its storied heritage with contemporary elegance across 115 suites.
pro_tip: Visit the Long Bar during off-peak afternoon hours (2-4 PM) to enjoy the original Singapore Sling experience without the evening crowds, and don't forget to throw your peanut shells on the floor – it's tradition!
dont_miss: The Writer's Bar showcases literary memorabilia from famous guests, while the hotel's museum displays fascinating artifacts. Take the complimentary heritage tour to discover hidden stories, and explore the adjacent shopping at Raffles City or the historic Raffles Landing Site just steps away.
pros: Legendary colonial heritage and iconic status as birthplace of the Singapore Sling
Exceptional butler service and world-class hospitality standards
Prime location in Singapore's cultural and business district
Luxurious all-suite accommodations with elegant furnishings
cons: High tourist traffic due to iconic status
